parts.name: Description
parts.description: An optional line under the title in smaller secondary text, for a place, a person or a status.

items.text: Use an Agenda for a short, read-only list of what happens when. For past events in order use Timeline; for rows with guests, a menu or a click, use Agenda Event.
Sort the items by time before you pass them in. The list renders them in array order and never reorders.
Use one short time format across the list, such as 09:30. The time column is 56 px wide, so a range such as 09:00 to 10:30 wraps onto a second line.
Set the colour to a CSS variable such as var(--brand-secondary), not a hex. Only a token follows the theme and dark mode.
Say what an entry is in its title or description, like Cancelled or Review. The bar is only a colour and does not reach people who cannot tell hues apart.
Don't make the Agenda clickable by wrapping it in a link or button. Rows have no hover or focus state; use Agenda Event when an entry opens something.
Don't put the Agenda inside another bordered card. It already has its own border and background, so a second box doubles the lines.

components.title: Action Bar
components.description: A bar of bulk actions for a selection. It sits where you place it, so fix it to the bottom of the page yourself if it should float.

parts.name: ActionBar
parts.description: The bar itself: a bordered card row with a shadow. It does not position or animate itself, so place it yourself, for example above a list or at the bottom of a table card.

parts.name: Label
parts.description: The text such as 3 selected, in 14 px medium. Without a label the separator goes too.

parts.name: Separator
parts.description: A 1 px vertical line between the label and the actions. It shows only when there is a label.

parts.name: Actions
parts.description: The buttons, in one row with an 8 px gap. Use small plain buttons and icon buttons; 8 px of right padding keeps a last icon button even.

items.text: Use an Action Bar for bulk actions on rows someone has selected: export, archive, delete. For actions that are always available, use Toolbar.
Show the bar only while something is selected and put the count in the label, like 3 selected. The count tells people what the buttons act on.
Keep to two to four actions that all make sense for any selection. Put the destructive one last.
Give icon-only buttons an aria-label. The bar has no name of its own, so each button must carry its own.
Place the bar yourself: above the list, or fixed and centred near the bottom. Reserve its room so content does not jump when it appears.
Switch to icon buttons on narrow screens. The bar does not wrap, and a label with three text buttons is wider than 320 px.
Don't run a destructive bulk action straight from the bar. Confirm it in an Alert Dialog that says how many items go, like Delete 3 invoices?
Don't use the bar for one-off page actions such as Save or Share. Those belong in the page header or a toolbar.
Don't leave the bar on screen when nothing is selected. A bar saying 0 selected with live buttons invites mistakes.

components.title: Carousel
components.description: A horizontally scrollable row of items with arrow controls.

props.name: autoPlay
props.description: Advances one slide every this many milliseconds and starts over after the last one. It stops while the pointer or the keyboard focus is inside, while the tab is hidden and with reduced motion. 0 or undefined turns it off.

props.name: drag
props.description: Drag the slides left or right with the mouse or a pen; touch already swipes. The row follows the pointer and, on release, springs to the nearest slide (a quick flick goes one slide further). Turn it off when the slides hold content that ne…

props.name: index
props.description: The slide the row shows, for dots and thumbnails that control it (controlled).

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the scrolling region.

props.name: navigationShape
props.description: Shape of the two arrow buttons: a rounded square or a circle.

props.name: onIndexChange
props.description: Called with the number of the slide the row now shows.

props.name: showArrows
props.description: Show the two arrow buttons. Turn them off when dots or thumbnails do the navigating.

props.name: slideSize
props.description: "auto" keeps every slide at its own width, "full" makes each slide as wide as the row.

keyboard: Tab to the slide strip, then Arrow Left / Right scroll it
Previous / Next buttons stay focusable at the ends (aria-disabled)
aria: role=region with aria-roledescription="carousel" and your label; slide changes are announced politely

parts.name: Carousel
parts.description: A row with a previous button, the slide strip and a next button. It snaps to each slide, takes the width of its parent and pauses autoplay while the pointer or focus is inside.

parts.name: Previous button
parts.description: A plain icon button on the left, square or round, that steps one slide back. It stays visible but disabled on the first slide, and is hidden but keeps its place when nothing overflows.

parts.name: Slide strip
parts.description: The focusable region, named by its label. It scrolls with arrow keys, swipes on touch and drags with a mouse or pen, and announces the visible items, such as 2 to 4 of 6, once a scroll stops.

parts.name: Slide
parts.description: Each child sits in a snap point. Slides keep their own width, or each fills the strip in full-width mode.

parts.name: Next button
parts.description: The same icon button on the right. It steps one slide forward and is disabled, not hidden, on the last slide.

items.text: Use a Carousel for a row of similar items people browse, such as project cards, screenshots or template previews. When every item matters or needs comparing, use a grid.
Set the label to what the row holds, such as Recent projects. The default Carousel tells nobody what is inside.
Keep the arrows beside the row. They never sit on top of a card, so a slide can hold its own buttons and links.
Drive dots, thumbnails or a counter through the index and its change handler instead of scrolling the strip yourself. The carousel springs to the slide and reports the one in view.
Show how many slides there are, with a counter like Slide 2 of 5, dots or thumbnails. Arrows alone do not tell people where they are.
Offer a pause button next to autoplay, and use autoplay for images, not text. It already pauses on hover, focus, a hidden tab and reduced motion, but moving slides are hard to read.
Don't put the only way to reach important content inside a carousel. People skip it, and a grid shows everything at once.
Don't leave drag on when slides hold controls that need the mouse, such as a slider. Turn it off; touch still swipes.
Don't autoplay in a dashboard or on a page people read. Moving content competes with the text.

components.title: Brand Logo
components.description: The logo of a product or service (Slack, GitHub, Stripe …) at 16, 20 or 24 px, for list rows, integrations and buttons.

props.name: name
props.description: Which brand.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name. Defaults to the brand name; pass "" when the text beside it already names the brand.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm` 16 px (beside small text and in buttons), `md` 20 px (default, list rows), `lg` 24 px.

props.name: name
props.description: Which product mark to draw.

parts.name: BrandLogo
parts.description: An svg with the image role and the brand's name, 16, 20 or 24 px. With label="" it is hidden from screen readers.

parts.name: BrandMark
parts.description: The bare mark on a 20 px grid, decorative unless it gets an aria-label. The same component as integration mark; integration logo puts it in a 36 px tile with a Tooltip.

items.text: Use Brand Logo to show which product a row, a card or an action is about: an integration, a connected account or a share target.
Pass label="" when the brand's name is written beside the logo, so a screen reader does not read it twice.
Use the 16 px size in buttons and beside small text, 20 px in list rows.
Don't recolour a logo or put it on a coloured tile. Brand colours are the brands' own; the one-colour logos already follow the text colour.
Don't use a brand logo for a payment method. Payment Logos draws Visa, Klarna and the others on their cards.
Don't use a logo alone as a button. Put it in a Button with a label, or give an Icon Button an aria-label.

components.title: Empty State
components.description: Placeholder shown when a list or search has no results.

props.name: variant
props.description: Frame style — mirrors the Figma Empty State "Style" variants.

parts.name: EmptyState
parts.description: A centred block of icon, title, description and action, with 40 px of padding. Four frames are available: dashed (the default), outline, none, or a muted background fill.

parts.name: Icon
parts.description: The icon, drawn in a round 48 px well at 24 px. Pass a Lucide icon.

parts.name: Title
parts.description: One short line on what is missing, such as No invoices yet. It renders as a paragraph, not a heading, so it does not change the outline of the page.

parts.name: Description
parts.description: The text under the title: why the place is empty, or what will appear here.

parts.name: Action
parts.description: Below the text, usually one Button that fills the empty place or undoes the filter. It takes any node, also a row of two buttons or a link.

items.text: Say what is missing, why and what to do next, then offer one action: No invoices yet, Invoices appear here as soon as the first one is sent, and New invoice.
For a search without results, name the query and offer a way out: No results for Anders, with a Clear search action.
For a failure, say what failed and offer the retry as the action: Couldn't load invoices with Try again. Show the pending state on the button while it runs.
Use the frameless look inside a card or panel that already has a border, and the dashed default where the empty state stands on the page.
Wrap an empty state that appears after typing in a status region, so a screen reader announces the change.
Don't show a bare No results line. Without a reason and a next step, an empty place looks broken and leaves people stuck.
Don't use it while data is still loading. A Skeleton shows that something is on its way; an empty state says that nothing is.
Don't offer two equal calls to action. One primary button, with at most a plain secondary one or a link to help.

components.title: File Tree
components.description: An indented list of folders and files: a tree with arrow-key navigation whose folders open and close, and onSelect reports the chosen file or folder.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name of the tree.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Called when a file or folder is activated (click, Enter or Space).

props.name: selectedId
props.description: The selected node (controlled). Without it the tree keeps its own selection.

keyboard: Tab: into the tree once (focused, selected or first row)
Arrow Up / Down: previous / next visible row; Home / End: first / last row
Arrow Right: open a folder, then into its first child; Arrow Left: close a folder, else go to its parent
Enter / Space: toggle a folder and select it, select a file; a letter jumps to the next row with that initial
aria: role=tree named by aria-label (default "Files"); rows role=treeitem with aria-level and aria-selected, folders aria-expanded
Children in role=group; rows of closed folders are inert and never hold focus

parts.name: FileTree
parts.description: A bordered panel that draws the data as rows, named Files by default. Top-level folders start open and deeper ones closed, and one row is the tab stop while the arrow keys move between visible rows.

parts.name: Folder row
parts.description: A tree item with a chevron, a folder icon and the name. Choosing it opens or closes its children and selects it; Right opens it or enters the first child, Left closes it.

parts.name: File row
parts.description: A tree item with a file icon and the name, cut with an ellipsis when too long. Choosing it selects it and calls your select handler, and the selected row has a subtle fill.

parts.name: Children
parts.description: The nested rows, indented one step per level. While closed they are inert and the arrow keys skip them, so focus never lands inside a closed folder.

items.text: Use a File Tree to show a folder structure people look through, such as the files of a template or an export. For items people search, sort or select in bulk, use Table.
Give every node a unique, stable id. It is the React key and the selection value, and a reused id mixes up which folders are open.
Mark a folder with a children array, even an empty one. A node without children is drawn as a file.
Keep the choice in your own state when something else on the page depends on it, such as an open file. Without it the tree keeps its own selection.
Name the tree with an aria-label when the page has more than one, such as Project files. The default name is Files.
Don't use it for multiple selection, drag and drop, renaming or icons per file type. It selects one row at a time and draws the same two icons.
Don't expect it to load children on demand. The tree draws the data it gets, so a folder that is still loading needs its own placeholder row.

components.title: Floating TOC
components.description: A table of contents for an article, with a marker that follows the section in view. It does not stick by itself: put it in a `sticky` container to keep it on screen.

props.name: scrollContainer
props.description: The element that scrolls the sections, if it is not the page.

parts.name: FloatingToc
parts.description: A nav named On this page with one link per section. It is not sticky itself, so place it in a sticky column.

parts.name: Entry
parts.description: A link to each section's id, indented 12 px per depth. The current one is darker and medium weight, and is marked as the current location.

parts.name: Active marker
parts.description: A 2 px bar on the left line that glides to the current entry. A fainter one previews the entry under the pointer or focus.

items.text: Use a Floating TOC beside a long page with several headed sections, such as documentation or a policy. For switching between separate views, use Tabs.
Give every section an id that matches its item. The links and the scroll spy find sections by that id, and a missing one is never marked.
Pass the scroll container when the sections scroll inside a panel rather than the page. Otherwise the spy watches the window and the marker stands still.
Put it in a sticky column yourself. The component draws the list and the marker, not its position.
Keep labels short, one line each, and in page order. A wrapped entry throws the marker out of line.
Leave the active section unset unless you track it yourself. Once you set it, the scroll spy is off and the marker stops following the reader.
Don't use it as the main navigation of a site. It lists the sections of one page and shows where the reader is.

components.title: Holo Card
components.description: A card with a soft glow that follows the mouse.

parts.name: HoloCard
parts.description: A card with a border, 16 px padding and a 16 px radius that clips its content. It tracks the pointer position for the glow, and you pass a class for the width.

parts.name: Glow
parts.description: A radial gradient 320 px across in the primary colour at 25 %, fading out. It fades in on hover, follows the pointer and sits behind the content; the figure keeps it on.

parts.name: Content
parts.description: The children, placed above the glow. Anything goes: text, an icon tile, a badge, buttons.

items.text: Use a Holo Card to make one or two showcase items stand out, such as a featured plan on a landing page. For everyday content and dashboard tiles, use Card.
Use it once or twice per view. When every card glows, none of them stands out.
Tint the glow by setting the primary colour on a wrapper, not with a gradient of your own. It follows brand and dark mode, and everything inside that uses the primary colour changes with it.
Keep the card complete without the glow. It appears only under a mouse pointer, so touch and keyboard users never need it.
Put a real link or Button inside for the action, and set the card's width with a class.
Don't rely on the glow to show the card is clickable. It is decoration with no focus state, no role and no tab stop.
Don't expect a tilt or 3D effect. The card never moves or rotates; only the glow under the pointer changes.

components.title: Item Card
components.description: A generic row card: icon, title, description, meta, action.

props.name: deletedAt
props.description: Type=trash — deletion line shown in red, no menu/checkbox.

props.name: thumbnail
props.description: Image preview instead of the icon tile.

props.name: color
props.description: Tint of the cover band.

props.name: cover
props.description: Icon, logo or image in the middle of the cover.

props.name: meta
props.description: One short line under the name.

props.name: deletedAt
props.description: Type=trash — deletion line shown in red, no menu/checkbox.

props.name: thumbnail
props.description: Image preview instead of the icon tile.

props.name: color
props.description: Tint of the cover band.

props.name: cover
props.description: Icon, logo or image in the middle of the cover.

props.name: meta
props.description: One short line under the name.

parts.name: ItemCard
parts.description: One framed row on the card surface: 1 px border, 8 px radius, 12 px padding and 12 px between its parts. It is a plain div with no hover, focus or click state of its own.

parts.name: Icon tile
parts.description: A 40 px indigo tint square with an 8 px radius and a 20 px icon in the tint text colour. It shows when you pass an icon.

parts.name: Title
parts.description: The title in 14 px semibold, cut to one line with an ellipsis.

parts.name: Description
parts.description: The description under the title in 13 px secondary text, also cut to one line.

parts.name: Meta
parts.description: A short fact on the right in 12 px tertiary text, such as a size or a date. It never shrinks, and a Badge works here too.

parts.name: Action
parts.description: One control at the far right, usually a Button or an icon button. It never shrinks and keeps its own focus and click behaviour.

parts.name: ItemCardGroup
parts.description: A bordered box with a 12 px radius and 8 px padding that stacks several cards 8 px apart, for a set that belongs together.

parts.name: ItemCardCover
parts.description: A clickable tile: a 96 px cover band in a tint, with an icon, logo or image in the middle, then the name and one line of detail. It is a button. It replaces ProjectCard.

parts.name: ItemCardFile
parts.description: A file tile: a 120 px preview (an icon on a tint, or an image), the name and the details, with an optional selection checkbox, a menu button and a deleted state. It replaces FileCard.

items.text: Use an ItemCard for an object on its own row, like a file, a connected app or a project, with one action. Use a Table for rows people compare by column and List View for a plain list in one frame.
Put the action in the action slot as a Button or icon button. The card takes no click handler, so the row itself isn't interactive.
Give an icon button an aria-label that names its object, such as More options for Checkout redesign, so the buttons of a set can be told apart.
Keep the title and description short, or give the full text another way. Both are cut to one line with an ellipsis.
Use the meta slot for a short fact with its unit, such as 2.4 MB or 2d ago, or for a status Badge.
Don't wrap each ItemCard in a Card. It draws its own border and padding; for a set, use ItemCardGroup.
Don't put more than one control in the action slot. Two buttons next to a long title leave no room for the text.

components.title: Timeline
components.description: A vertical sequence of dated, dot-connected events.

props.name: compact
props.description: Smaller dots and text, for milestones and long lists.

props.name: orientation
props.description: "vertical" stacks the entries, "horizontal" lays them out in a row with the time above each dot.

props.name: avatar
props.type: { src?: string; initials?: string; color?: AvatarColor }
props.description: Actor avatar (Type=event).

props.name: badge
props.description: Trailing badge/label on the title row (Type=step).

props.name: children
props.description: Extra content below the title (comment excerpt, reactions, attachments …).

props.name: last
props.description: The last entry of the list: no connector line below it.

props.name: object
props.description: Small object chip under the title (Type=event) — e.g. project name.

props.name: status
props.description: Status dot (Type=step): tone + icon.

props.name: avatar
props.type: { src?: string; initials?: string; color?: AvatarColor }
props.description: Actor avatar (Type=event).

props.name: badge
props.description: Trailing badge/label on the title row (Type=step).

props.name: children
props.description: Extra content below the title (comment excerpt, reactions, attachments …).

props.name: last
props.description: The last entry of the list: no connector line below it.

props.name: object
props.description: Small object chip under the title (Type=event) — e.g. project name.

props.name: status
props.description: Status dot (Type=step): tone + icon.

parts.name: Timeline
parts.description: Draws the entries, stacked in a column or laid out in a row, and joins them with a line. Compact makes dots, text and gaps smaller, and it is a plain div, not a list.

parts.name: Dot
parts.description: The marker of an entry: a 24 px circle (16 px when compact) in the entry's colour, with an icon or a small point inside. An avatar replaces it.

parts.name: Title
parts.description: The title of the entry in semibold text. It can be any React node, so keep it to a short sentence.

parts.name: Timestamp
parts.description: The timestamp in small tertiary text, printed as written. It sits next to the title in a column and above the dot in a row.

parts.name: Description
parts.description: The detail of the entry, in secondary text under the title.

parts.name: Connector
parts.description: A 1 px line in the border colour from one dot to the next. The last entry has none, and it isn't numbered because it runs between two dots.

items.text: Pass a stable id for every entry. It is the React key, so a list that grows at the top keeps its rows.
Give every timestamp a date or a time with its unit, such as Nov 9, 09:14 or 3 min ago. It prints as written, so format it yourself and use one style in the whole list.
Say the status in words, in the title or description: Tests failed, not just a red dot. Colour and icon are decoration for people who can see them.
Pass dot colours as tokens, such as var(--success) or var(--destructive). The glyph inside switches between white and dark so it stays readable.
Use compact for long lists and for a Timeline inside a small card. Dots, text and gaps shrink so more entries fit.
Don't use a horizontal Timeline for more than four or five entries. Each entry gets an equal share of the width, so a long row squeezes the text.
Don't put long paragraphs, buttons or links in the title or description. For one rich entry with a comment, object chip or attachments, use a Timeline Event.
Don't write times like recently or a while ago. People can't tell which entry came first.

components.title: Widget
components.description: A generic dashboard widget shell: header, body, footer.

parts.name: Widget
parts.description: The frame of one dashboard tile: a bordered card with a 16 px radius, 16 px of padding and 16 px between header, body and footer.

parts.name: Header
parts.description: A row with the title and description on the left and the action on the right. It only renders when there is a title or an action, so a description alone doesn't show.

parts.name: Title
parts.description: The title as an h3 in bold 16 px text, so heading order stays intact under a level-two page heading.

parts.name: Description
parts.description: The description under the title in small secondary text: the period, scope or unit of the data.

parts.name: Action
parts.description: The action at the right end of the header, usually a plain View all button or an icon button with an aria-label.

parts.name: Body
parts.description: The content. The body grows to fill the tile, so in a grid row the footers of tiles with different bodies line up at the bottom.

parts.name: Footer
parts.description: The footer below a divider line: a note on the data such as Updated 2 minutes ago, or one link.

items.text: Put widgets under a level-two page heading. The title renders as an h3, so the heading order stays intact.
Keep the header to one action, such as a plain View all button or an icon button with an aria-label. More than one belongs in a menu.
Keep the frame in loading, empty and error states and swap only the body. The tile keeps its title and place, so the page doesn't jump.
Set the width on the box around the Widget or with a class. It fills its container, so a grid cell or a maximum width decides how wide it is.
Use the footer for a note about the data or one link, such as Updated 2 minutes ago or Manage plan.
Don't set a description without a title or an action. The header isn't rendered then, so the description doesn't appear.
Don't put a Card or another bordered box in the body. The Widget is already the frame, so use rows, dividers and Progress bars inside it.
Don't use a Widget for content with media, a custom header or one press target for the whole tile. Use a Card.

components.title: Segment
components.description: A single-select toggle group, like a compact tab bar, with a pill or a rounded-corner track.

props.name: activation
props.description: `auto` (default): the arrow keys move focus and choose the option. `manual`: the arrow keys, Home and End only move focus; Enter or Space chooses. Use it where a wrong choice has a cost (a permission, a payment).

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Names the group for screen readers, e.g. "Version".

props.name: shape
props.description: `pill` (default) or `rounded` for the square-cornered version.

props.name: slide
props.description: The selected option's pill slides to the next option instead of switching. It moves with `transform` only (the pill is laid out at its final size and animated from the old one), so it costs no layout, and it stays put when the user prefers…

props.name: wrap
props.description: The options wrap to a second row when the track is wider than its container (a phone) instead of running past the edge. One row looks the same as without it. Off by default.

parts.name: Segment
parts.description: The track: a grey bar, as wide as its options, labelled for assistive technology. Size sets its height, and shape sets the corners: a full pill, or 8 px with concentric options.

parts.name: Option
parts.description: One button per entry in the options array, with the selected option as the single tab stop. Hover uses the page fill, pressed the subtle fill, and a disabled option is dimmed and skipped by keys.

parts.name: Selected pill
parts.description: The white pill behind the selected option, drawn only when sliding is on, and it moves from the old option to the new one. Without sliding the selected option paints the white fill itself.

parts.name: Icon
parts.description: An icon you pass with an option, shown before the label at 14 or 16 px. Give a Lucide icon a 1.5 stroke, and it takes its option's text colour.

items.text: Use it to switch the view or scope of one piece of content: day, week, month, list or grid, monthly or yearly. For separate panels use Tabs, and for on or off use a switch.
Keep it to two to five options with short labels. The track does not wrap or scroll, so five long labels are wider than a phone.
Pass an aria-label, for example Time range. It names the tab list, and the options only carry their own labels.
Give an icon-only option a visually hidden label such as List. Without it the option has no accessible name.
Pick the size by place: the smaller ones inside a card or chart header, the larger ones to line up with a Button. Those heights follow the density tokens.
Turn on sliding when the options are neighbours the eye should follow, such as a period. Use the plain version for a control that changes rarely.
Don't pass a value that matches no option. The first enabled option becomes the tab stop, but none looks selected.
Don't use a Segment to open panels with their own content and URL, because it renders no panels. Tabs owns the panels.
Switch to manual activation when a choice is hard to undo or costly, such as a permission level or billing interval. Keep the default when choosing only changes a view.

components.title: Select
components.description: A styled select: a full-width field trigger, or a compact inline trigger that sits within a sentence, with a popup list.

props.name: actionsRef
props.description: A ref to imperative actions. - `unmount`: Manually unmounts the select. Call this after any externally controlled closing animation finishes.

props.name: autoComplete
props.description: Provides a hint to the browser for autofill.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether the select popup is initially open. To render a controlled select popup, use the `open` prop instead.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The uncontrolled value of the select when it's initially rendered. To render a controlled select, use the `value` prop instead.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether the component should ignore user interaction.

props.name: form
props.description: Identifies the form that owns the hidden input. Useful when the select is rendered outside the form.

props.name: highlightItemOnHover
props.description: Whether moving the pointer over items should highlight them. Disabling this prop allows CSS `:hover` to be differentiated from the `:focus` (`data-highlighted`) state.

props.name: id
props.description: The id of the Select.

props.name: inputRef
props.description: A ref to access the hidden input element.

props.name: isItemEqualToValue
props.description: Custom comparison logic used to determine if a select item value matches the current selected value. Useful when item values are objects without matching referentially. Defaults to `Object.is` comparison.

props.name: items
props.type: Record<string, React.ReactNode> | ReadonlyArray<{ label: React.ReactNode; value: any; }> | ReadonlyArray<Group<any>>
props.description: Data structure of the items rendered in the select popup. When specified, `<Select.Value>` renders the label of the selected item instead of the raw value.

props.name: itemToStringLabel
props.description: When the item values are objects (`<Select.Item value={object}>`), this function converts the object value to a string representation for display in the trigger. If the shape of the object is `{ value, label }`, the label will be used auto…

props.name: itemToStringValue
props.description: When the item values are objects (`<Select.Item value={object}>`), this function converts the object value to a string representation for form submission. If the shape of the object is `{ value, label }`, the value will be used automatical…

props.name: modal

parts.name: Select
parts.description: The root. It holds the chosen value and open state and renders nothing itself, and it reads option labels from its items, so the field shows Germany for the value de before the list ever opens.

parts.name: SelectTrigger
parts.description: The field: a button that shows the chosen option and opens the list, 36 px high with an indigo border while open. Give it a visible label or an aria-label.

parts.name: SelectValue
parts.description: The text in the field: the chosen option's label, or the placeholder in a quieter colour while nothing is chosen. An option with an icon shows the icon here too.

parts.name: Chevron
parts.description: The 16 px chevron at the right of the field. It is part of the trigger and hidden from assistive technology.

parts.name: SelectContent
parts.description: The list panel. It opens below the field at the same width and scrolls when it runs out of room, and its 12 px corner is concentric with the 8 px rows inside its 4 px padding.

parts.name: SelectItem
parts.description: One option, 32 px high. Its value is what the select holds and its children are the label, with an optional icon in front; the highlighted option gets the page fill.

parts.name: Check
parts.description: A 16 px check at the right of the chosen option.

items.text: Give the select a visible label, joined to the trigger with an id. The placeholder is a hint such as Select a status, not the name of the field.
Set a placeholder for a field that starts empty and say what is wanted: Select a status, not just Select.
Keep the labels short and parallel. The list is as wide as the field, and a long label is cut off.
Mark an invalid select as invalid on the trigger, and say why in a line under it, linked with aria-describedby.
Don't use it for a long list. Past a dozen options people scroll instead of reading; a Combobox lets them type.
Don't use it for two or three options that fit on the screen. Radio buttons show every option at once and need one click less.
Don't use it for actions. Choosing an option sets a value; a menu of actions belongs in a Dropdown Menu.

Inline: Give every trigger an aria-label that names what is chosen, such as Sort order or Status of WUI-482. There is no visible label, and the announced value alone doesn't say what the choice is for.
Inline: Don't use it as a form field. Without a border it doesn't look like an input; use Select with a label inside a Field.
Inline: Don't let long labels push the sentence around. The trigger is as wide as the current label, so text after it moves when the value changes; keep labels about the same length.

components.title: Checkbox Button Group
components.description: A multi-select group of toggle-styled buttons.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class applied to the element, or a function that returns a class based on the component's state.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The pressed state of the toggle group represented by an array of the values of all pressed toggle buttons. This is the uncontrolled counterpart of `value`.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether the toggle group should ignore user interaction.

props.name: loopFocus
props.description: Whether to loop keyboard focus back to the first item when the end of the list is reached while using the arrow keys.

props.name: multiple
props.description: When `false` only one item in the group can be pressed. If any item in the group becomes pressed, the others will become unpressed. When `true` multiple items can be pressed.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Callback fired when the pressed states of the toggle group changes.

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

props.name: style
props.description: Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state.

props.name: value
props.description: The pressed state of the toggle group represented by an array of the values of all pressed toggle buttons. This is the controlled counterpart of `defaultValue`.

parts.name: CheckboxButtonGroup
parts.description: A wrapping row of toggle buttons where any number can be on, with an 8 px gap. The value is the list of buttons that are on, and the group needs an aria-label.

parts.name: ToggleButton
parts.description: One button, on or off, with its own value. It shows the pressed state in the indigo tint, and an icon-only button needs an aria-label.

parts.name: Mark
parts.description: The 16 px checkbox square before the label, with a check while the button is on. It is drawn for buttons with a text label and left out for icon-only ones, and you can hide it.

parts.name: Icon
parts.description: An optional Lucide icon before the label, 16 px with a 1.5 stroke. It takes the text colour of the button, so it turns indigo with the label.

items.text: Use CheckboxButtonGroup for a few short options that can be combined, like text styles or filters. For one choice use RadioButtonGroup, and for long options use Checkbox or Selector Item.
Pick the group by what the options mean. CheckboxButtonGroup is a set of toggles where any number can be on, while RadioButtonGroup is one choice that arrow keys select and cannot be cleared.
Keep the value as an array of strings and update it in the change handler. Wrapping on narrow screens is built in, so no custom breakpoints are needed.
Name the group with a visible label and aria-labelledby, or with an aria-label. A screen reader announces the name when focus enters the group.
Give every icon-only ToggleButton an aria-label such as Bold. The pressed state is announced, but the icon alone has no name.
Put the error on the group: mark it invalid and write one message under it. Do not repeat the message on every button.
Don't use it for options with a sentence of explanation. A button holds a word or two, so use a Checkbox or Selector Item with a description.
Don't set the vertical orientation without stacking the buttons, or arrow keys will move in a direction the layout does not show.
Don't use it to switch between views or pages. People expect a Segment or Tabs for that.

components.title: Radio Button Group
components.description: A single-select group of toggle-styled buttons.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class applied to the element, or a function that returns a class based on the component's state.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The pressed state of the toggle group represented by an array of the values of all pressed toggle buttons. This is the uncontrolled counterpart of `value`.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether the toggle group should ignore user interaction.

props.name: loopFocus
props.description: Whether to loop keyboard focus back to the first item when the end of the list is reached while using the arrow keys.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Callback fired when the pressed states of the toggle group changes.

props.name: orientation
props.description: The direction the arrow keys move in. `both` (default) works like native radios: Right and Down go to the next button, Left and Up to the previous one. `horizontal` listens to Left and Right only, `vertical` to Up and Down only.

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

props.name: style
props.description: Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state.

props.name: value
props.description: The pressed state of the toggle group represented by an array of the values of all pressed toggle buttons. This is the controlled counterpart of `defaultValue`.

parts.name: RadioButtonGroup
parts.description: A wrapping row of buttons with an 8 px gap, where one is chosen once the person has chosen. It is a radio group: name it with an aria-label, and mark the whole group invalid if needed.

parts.name: ToggleButton
parts.description: One button with its own value. In this group it is a radio, and a chosen one takes the indigo tint; icon-only buttons need an aria-label.

parts.name: Mark
parts.description: The 16 px radio circle in front of the label, with a 6 px dot while the button is chosen. It is drawn for buttons with a text label and left out for icon-only ones; you can hide it.

parts.name: Icon
parts.description: An optional Lucide icon before the label, 16 px at a 1.5 stroke. It takes the text colour of the button, so it turns indigo with the label.

items.text: Use it for one choice from a few short options that should be one click away, such as a billing period. For options with a description use Radio Group; for combining options use CheckboxButtonGroup.
Keep the value as an array and read the choice from its first entry. It has one entry once a button is chosen and never becomes empty by a press, so no guard for an empty choice is needed.
Name the group with a visible label and aria-labelledby, or with an aria-label. A screen reader announces the name when focus enters the group.
Give every icon-only button an aria-label such as Align left. A screen reader announces the label and whether the radio is chosen; the icon alone has no name.
Choose a sensible default when one exists, and show what the choice changes right next to the group.
Use CheckboxButtonGroup when people may choose several options or none. The two look alike but behave differently: this one is a radio group, the other a set of toggles.
Don't use two buttons for on and off. A single setting that is on or off is a Switch or a Toggle.
Don't use it for more than about five options or for options that need a sentence of explanation. Use a Radio Group or a Select instead.
Don't use it to switch between views or pages. People expect a Segment or Tabs for that.

components.title: Number Stepper
components.description: A +/- increment control for a bounded numeric value.

props.name: format
props.description: Formats the displayed value, e.g. `(n) => `${n}%``

keyboard: Tab to the Decrease / Increase buttons, Enter / Space to step
aria: role=group; the value is announced politely (aria-live) when it changes
The buttons carry aria-label "Decrease" / "Increase"

parts.name: NumberStepper
parts.description: A group holding a minus button, the number and a plus button, 8 px apart. It is controlled with a value and a change handler, and it has no visible label, so give it an aria-label.

parts.name: Decrease button
parts.description: A 32 px plain icon button named Decrease. At the minimum it dims to 40% but stays focusable, so repeated Enter does not drop focus to the page.

parts.name: Value
parts.description: The number between the buttons, at least 32 px wide, semibold with tabular figures so it does not jiggle. It is announced politely when it changes.

parts.name: Increase button
parts.description: A 32 px plain icon button named Increase. It dims and stops at the maximum in the same way.

items.text: Name the group with an aria-label such as Adults or Quantity of canvas tote bags. The buttons only say Decrease and Increase; the group name tells a screen reader what they change.
Set min, max and step to the real limits, so the buttons stop where the values stop. The value never leaves the range.
Use the format function to add the unit, such as 15 min, so the number is not read without it.
Say why a limit was reached when it is not obvious, such as Only 5 in stock. A dimmed button alone does not explain itself.
Don't use it for a value people may want to type, such as 250. There is no text entry, so 1 to 250 takes 249 presses: use Number Field.
Don't expect arrow keys to work. It is two buttons, not a spin button, so Tab reaches each and Enter or Space presses it; use Number Field where arrow keys, Home and End matter.
Don't use it for a range where the position matters more than the number. A Slider shows where the value sits between the limits.
Don't show the number in the stepper and again in a label next to it. One place for the value is enough.

components.title: Drop Zone
components.description: A drag-and-drop file upload target with a click-to-browse fallback.

props.name: hint
props.description: Line under the prompt. Defaults to the accepted types, or "Any file type". State your size limit here.

keyboard: Tab to the hidden file input (the zone shows the focus ring), Space / Enter opens the file dialog
aria: A label around a native file input; the hint text is linked with aria-describedby

parts.name: DropZone
parts.description: A label with a 2 px dashed border around a real file input. A drop anywhere on it, or a click, hands the files to your handler, and while a file is dragged over it the border and fill turn indigo.

parts.name: Icon
parts.description: An upload icon in the tertiary text colour. It is decorative and hidden from assistive technology.

parts.name: Prompt
parts.description: The line Drop files here or browse. It is the visible name of the control.

parts.name: Browse link
parts.description: The word browse in the link colour. It is not a separate button: a click anywhere on the zone opens the file dialog.

parts.name: Hint
parts.description: The small line under the prompt, by default the accepted types or Any file type. It is where a size limit belongs and the accessible description of the file input.

parts.name: File input
parts.description: The real file input, visually hidden and always accepting several files. It takes the keyboard focus, and the focus ring is drawn around the whole zone.

items.text: State the limit in the hint, for example PNG, JPG or PDF up to 10 MB. The zone does not enforce a size, so say what you will check.
Show every file in a list under the zone, with name, size, a progress bar while it uploads and a Remove or Cancel action. The zone itself shows no files.
Say in words why a file was refused, for example that the type is not supported and which types work. Keep the row so people see which file it was.
Check the type and size of every file in your file handler. A drop passes every file, whatever the accept setting says.
Don't rely on accept to keep wrong files out. It only filters the file dialog, and a dropped file of any type still reaches your handler.
Don't make drag and drop the only way in. The zone also opens the file dialog on a click and on Enter or Space, so keep that path working.
Don't put the zone inside another clickable element, such as a button or a link. It is already a label around an input, and the click would count twice.
Don't use it for a single file in a tight form row. A Button that opens the file dialog takes less room and reads as a form control.

components.title: Rich Text Editor
components.description: A Tiptap-powered WYSIWYG editor with a formatting toolbar.

props.name: aria-describedby
props.description: Id of the element that describes the editing area, such as a helper line.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name of the editing area when there is no visible label.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Id of the element that names the editing area, such as a visible label.

props.name: id
props.description: Id of the editing area. A `<label htmlFor>` cannot name it (it is not a form control): use `aria-labelledby`.

props.name: slashMenu
props.description: Typing "/" at the start of a line or after a space opens a block menu at the caret: arrow keys pick, Enter or Tab inserts, Escape closes, typing filters. `true` shows the default blocks (headings, lists, task, quote, divider, code); pass y…

parts.name: RichTextEditor
parts.description: A 16 px frame with a 1 px border around the toolbar and the editing area. It loads its engine (Tiptap) on first render, shows a skeleton until then and gets an indigo ring on focus.

parts.name: RichTextEditorSkeleton
parts.description: The empty frame with the placeholder that shows until the editor has loaded, 38 px of toolbar and 128 px of text. Export it for your own loading state.

parts.name: Toolbar
parts.description: A row of 28 px icon buttons in 6 px of padding with a 2 px gap, closed off from the text by a 1 px line. The buttons are Bold, Italic, Underline, Bulleted list, Numbered list and Link.

parts.name: Toolbar button
parts.description: A 28 px icon button with an 8 px corner. It is a toggle, shown pressed while the cursor is in text with that format, and Link asks for the address in the browser's prompt.

parts.name: Separator
parts.description: A 1 px line, 20 px high, between the text styles, the lists and the link.

parts.name: Editing area
parts.description: The editable text: a multi-line textbox at least 128 px tall with 12 px padding that grows with its content. While empty it shows the placeholder, and you name it with an aria-label.

items.text: Use a Rich Text Editor for text that people format: a note, a project description, a reply, release notes. For plain text use a Textarea; for a message to an AI assistant use a Prompt Input.
Name the editing area with aria-labelledby pointing to a visible Label, or an aria-label when there is no room. A label with htmlFor cannot reach it, because the area is not a form control.
Store the HTML from the change handler and pass it back as the content when the person returns. The content is the starting text only, so use a new key to load other content.
Sanitize the HTML on your server before you store it or show it to other people. The editor limits the tags it produces, but a server should never trust the browser.
Say what is wrong next to the editor and keep the text. The editor has no invalid state of its own, so colour the frame with the error border and link the message with aria-describedby.

Turn on slashMenu for longer documents such as notes and briefs: "/" opens a block menu at the caret (headings, lists, task, quote, divider, code). Keep it off for short replies, where the toolbar is enough.
Don't use it for text that must stay plain, such as a name, a title or a search term. The output is HTML, not plain text, and a one-line Input is easier to fill in.
Don't use it as the composer of an AI chat. That is a Prompt Input: it sends on Enter, grows with the message and has attach and send buttons, not a formatting toolbar.
Don't rely on a shortcut for the link. There is none: the toolbar button is the way to add or remove a link.

components.title: Color Picker
components.description: Pick a colour: saturation and brightness, hue, opacity, eyedropper, HEX/RGB/HSL values and saved colours — inline or from a trigger field.

props.name: alpha
props.description: Opacity, 0–1. Leave out `onAlphaChange` and `alpha` to hide the opacity slider.

props.name: format
props.description: The value fields' format; the select in the picker switches it.

props.name: onClose
props.description: Shows the close button.

props.name: swatches
props.description: Saved colours; the + adds the current colour.

props.name: title
props.description: Heading of the panel. Hidden when `null`.

props.name: value
props.description: The colour as #RRGGBB.

props.name: variant
props.description: How a colour is picked: a saturation/brightness area or a grid of swatches.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether the popover is open by default.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the field.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the popover opens or closes.

props.name: open
props.description: The popover is open. Controlled; leave out for the field to manage it.

props.name: pickerProps
props.description: Everything else the picker takes (alpha, swatches, format …).

props.name: shape
props.description: `default`: the Input-sized field with a square swatch. `pill`: a 32 px pill with a colour dot, to sit in a row of pill-shaped colour presets.

keyboard: Arrow keys: move the saturation/brightness handle and the hue slider
aria: The handles are role=slider with aria-valuetext; swatches are options in a listbox

parts.name: ColorPicker
parts.description: A 296 px wide card with a title, a colour area, hue and opacity sliders, value fields and saved colours. It holds the colour as a hex string and the opacity from 0 to 1, and it is not a native input.

parts.name: Header
parts.description: The title, Color picker by default, and a close button at the right when a close handler is set. Setting the title to null removes the title, and the whole header if there is no close handler.

parts.name: Colour area
parts.description: A two-dimensional slider: saturation runs left to right and brightness bottom to top. The grid variant is a grid of greys and nine shades of twelve hues, with arrow keys moving between swatches.

parts.name: Hue and opacity
parts.description: Two sliders under the area, with an eyedropper button at the left in browsers that have one. The opacity slider and field can be left out.

parts.name: Value
parts.description: A select for the format (HEX, RGB or HSL) and the fields for the value, followed by the opacity in percent. A field commits on Enter or blur, so typing 2 on the way to 255 does not move the colour.

parts.name: Saved colours
parts.description: A row of 24 px swatches with a plus button that saves the current colour. The chosen swatch gets a ring in its own colour, and you can set the first set or control the whole list.

parts.name: ColorPickerTrigger
parts.description: A field that opens the picker in a popover below it: a swatch, the hex value and a chevron, the size of an Input. The pill shape is a 32 px pill with a colour dot, for a row of presets.

items.text: Use ColorPickerTrigger in a form or a settings row. The field shows the colour at rest, and the panel opens only when it is needed.
Use ColorPicker on the page when the colour is the task, for example an editor with a preview beside it. Judge the colour on real content, not on a bare swatch.
Hold the colour as a hex string and the opacity as a number, each with its change handler. Leave opacity out where a colour is always opaque.
Pass the colours of your product as the default swatches, so people start from a palette they should use.
Give the trigger a label, such as Primary colour. Its accessible name is the label plus the value, because a swatch alone says nothing to a screen reader.
Don't use a native color input. Its panel is the browser's own and cannot carry your tokens, your saved colours or an opacity.
Don't use a colour as the only information. A picked colour needs its value in text, as the field and the preview line show.
Don't use it to choose from a short list of fixed colours. A row of Selector Items or a Radio Button Group is quicker and keeps people inside your palette.

components.title: Cell Color Picker
components.description: A compact color swatch picker for inline use in a Data Table cell.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Name for screen readers, such as "Label colour". The accessible name becomes "Label colour, #6366F1". Default: "Colour #6366F1. Choose a colour".

parts.name: Table
parts.description: The table the cell sits in. The first column holds the row names, the header row names the columns, and the picker lives in a table cell.

parts.name: Column header
parts.description: The header of the colour column. It says what the colour is for, such as Colour or Chart colour.

parts.name: Row header
parts.description: The first cell of the row, marked as the row header, which says which label, calendar or series the colour belongs to. Give the swatch the same name as its aria-label.

parts.name: CellColorPicker
parts.description: A round swatch button that opens a six-colour popover. Built for a table cell, it returns the chosen colour as a hex string, and you hold the value and write it back on change.

parts.name: Swatch button
parts.description: The 24 px round trigger filled with the current colour. Its name is the label plus the hex value, and it announces a dialog.

parts.name: Popover
parts.description: The popover with the six swatches in one row. Its name comes from the aria-label, Choose a colour by default, and it stays open after a choice.

parts.name: Swatch
parts.description: One of the six colour buttons in the popover, named by its hex value. The active one has a ring and is marked pressed.

items.text: Keep the value as a hex string and store it in the change handler. The trigger names itself with that value.
Pass an aria-label that names the row, such as Billing colour, so the swatch reads Billing colour plus its hex value. Mark the first cell of each row as a row header too.
Show the effect of the choice nearby, such as a legend bar or a preview, so nobody judges the colour from a 24 px circle alone.
Give the colour column a header that says what the colour is for, and centre the swatch in a narrow column.
Don't expect colours outside the six swatches. Another value still shows on the trigger, but no swatch is marked and people can only pick from the six.
Don't use it outside a table row, since it is 24 px wide and has no visible label. Use ColorPicker for a labelled field with hex entry and opacity.
Don't use colour as the only carrier of meaning. Pair it with the name of the label or series, as the row header does.
Don't expect the Figma Editable Cell states (Edit, Changed, Saving, Error, Disabled). It only has a value and a change handler.

components.title: Cell Slider
components.description: A compact progress/value slider for inline use in a Data Table cell.

parts.name: Table
parts.description: The table the cell sits in. The first column holds the row names, the header row names the columns, and the bar lives in a table cell.

parts.name: Column header
parts.description: The header of the bar column. It names the measure and the unit, such as Quota used, because the bar itself has no label.

parts.name: Row header
parts.description: The first cell of the row, marked as the row header. It says whose level the bar shows.

parts.name: CellSlider
parts.description: A small bar, 112 px wide, with a number beside it. It shows a value out of a maximum (default 100) and cannot be dragged, since it is a display, not a control.

parts.name: Track
parts.description: The 4 px grey bar with fully rounded ends. It always spans the width left of the number.

parts.name: Fill
parts.description: The primary-coloured part of the track. Its width is the value divided by the maximum, capped at 100 %.

parts.name: Number
parts.description: The raw value to the right of the bar, 12 px and right-aligned in 28 px, so the bar never has to be read on its own.

items.text: Set the maximum to the real ceiling, such as 5 for a 5-point score or the seat limit of the row. The fill is clamped to the track, but the number still shows the raw value.
Put it in a column whose header names the measure and the unit, such as Quota used. The bar and number have no label or role of their own.
Mark the first cell of each row as a row header, so the number is read with its row.
Pair it with a control when the level can change, such as a button that completes a task. The slider then follows the value.
Don't build an editable cell around it. It has no handler, keyboard support or ARIA role, so use a Slider with an aria-label in the cell instead.
Don't use it for one task or upload with a label and a status. Progress has the role and the text for that.
Don't rely on the bar for values outside 0 to the maximum. It draws an empty or full bar there, and only the number shows the real figure.
Don't count on the Figma Editable Cell Slider states (View, Edit, Changed, Saving, Error, Disabled). The React cell shows a level only.

components.title: Cell Select
components.description: A compact select for inline use in a Data Table cell.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Name for screen readers — a combobox is not named by its current value.

parts.name: Table
parts.description: The table the cell sits in. The first column holds the row names, the header row names the columns, and the select lives in a table cell.

parts.name: Row header
parts.description: The first cell of the row, marked as the row header. It says which row the select belongs to, so a screen reader reads it with the select.

parts.name: CellSelect
parts.description: A compact select for a table cell: a 32 px trigger, 128 px wide, with a plain list of strings as options. You hold the value and write it back on change.

parts.name: Trigger
parts.description: The button that shows the current value and opens the list. It has no visible label, so give it an aria-label (default Choose a value).

parts.name: Value
parts.description: The current value on one line in 12 px text. A value longer than the trigger is cut with an ellipsis.

parts.name: Chevron
parts.description: The down chevron at the right edge of the trigger. It stays inside the border at every value length.

parts.name: Options list
parts.description: The popup under the trigger, as wide as the trigger. A long option wraps onto more lines here, so the full text is always readable.

parts.name: Option
parts.description: One row of the list for each option string. The highlighted option takes the page background and the chosen one shows a check.

items.text: Set an aria-label per row and column, such as Role of Nora Lindgren. A trigger that shows only its value does not name itself to a screen reader.
Pass options as the exact strings you store, and keep the value one of them. The value is the text, with no separate label.
Keep options short, up to about 14 characters. The trigger shows one line in 128 px and cuts the rest with an ellipsis.
Mark the first cell of each row as a row header, so a screen reader reads the row, the column and the value together.
Don't use it for long lists or options that need a description. It has no search or groups, so use a Combobox.
Don't use it in a form with a label. There NativeSelect with its Label and helper text is the right control.
Don't pass a value that is not in the options. No option is checked and the list has no starting point.
Don't expect a saving, error or disabled look. CellSelect has no such props, unlike the Editable Cell states in Figma.

components.title: Cell Switch
components.description: A compact switch for inline use in a Data Table cell.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Name for screen readers — a cell has no visible label of its own.

parts.name: Table
parts.description: The table the cell sits in. The first column holds the row names, the header row names the columns, and the switch lives in a table cell.

parts.name: Column header
parts.description: The header of the switch column. It says what the switch changes, such as Email alerts, and aligns the same way as the cell.

parts.name: Row header
parts.description: The first cell of the row, marked as the row header. It says whose or which setting this is, so a screen reader reads it with the switch.

parts.name: CellSwitch
parts.description: A Switch with a default aria-label of Toggle, made for a table cell with no visible label. You hold the checked state and write it back on change.

parts.name: Track
parts.description: The 32 by 18 px pill. It is brand-coloured when on and grey when off, and it carries the switch role and checked state.

parts.name: Knob
parts.description: The 16 px circle that slides from one end of the track to the other. It swings slightly past the end before it settles.

items.text: Name every switch by its row and column, such as Email alerts for Nora Lindgren. The default Toggle is the same in every row and tells a screen-reader user nothing.
Mark the first cell of each row as a row header and give the switch column a header that says what it changes. The cell is then read as row, column and state.
Keep the checked state in your own state and save in the same handler that writes it back. The cell keeps no state.
Align the switch like its column header: centred in a narrow column, left beside text. Use the same alignment class on the header and the cell.
Don't use CellSwitch outside a table. Without a visible label the switch has no context, so use Switch with a Label, or a Selector Item.
Don't use a switch for an action that needs a confirmation, such as deleting data. A switch applies at once.
Don't put two switches in one cell. One cell holds one value, so give each value its own column.
Don't expect a saving, error or disabled look from CellSwitch. For rows that need them, use a Switch with those states inside the cell.

components.title: Selector Item
components.description: A list row pairing a leading icon/avatar and label/description with a trailing radio, checkbox, or switch.

props.name: action
props.description: Secondary action beside the row. Rendered outside the label; clicking it never toggles the control.

props.name: announceError
props.description: Announce the error at once (`role="alert"`). Set it only for an error that appears after an action such as a failed submit; leave it off for an error that is already there when the page loads, or it is read twice.

props.name: badge
props.description: Small pill next to the title, for example "Recommended".

props.name: control
props.description: The RadioGroupItem, Checkbox or Switch of the row. Not needed (and ignored) when `href` is set.

props.name: controlPosition
props.description: Which side of the label the control sits on.

props.name: error
props.description: Error text below the row; marks the control invalid. It is linked with aria-describedby, so a screen reader reads it when the control gets focus.

props.name: helper
props.description: Hint text below the row.

props.name: href
props.description: Link mode: the whole row is an anchor with a trailing chevron and no control.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon in a 40 px tint-indigo tile, in front of the text (no rim). Ignored when `leading` is set.

props.name: layout
props.description: `card` is the bordered row; `inline` is a 24 px row without border or padding.

props.name: metadata
props.description: Short secondary text next to the control (a price, a count). Not interactive.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Link mode: called on click. Without a real `href` the click does not jump to "#".

props.name: selected
props.description: Shows the selected look without a checked control, for example the current choice of a link list. A checked control does it on its own.

props.name: aria-describedby
props.description: Extra description for the control, for example the id of a hint under the row.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Names the control (radio, checkbox) or the link when the row has no visible text to name it.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Names the control by another element, for a row whose label is somewhere else.

props.name: badge
props.description: Small badge next to the title, e.g. "Recommended"

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dims the row once (the row, not its control as well), turns the control or link off and takes it out of the arrow-key order. A disabled `OptionRowGroup` disables every row in it.

props.name: icon
props.description: Leading icon (rendered in a 40px tint-indigo tile with a tint-text rim for variant="icon")

props.name: value
props.description: Required for radio/checkbox variants — the RadioGroupItem / Checkbox value.

props.name: variant
props.description: radio (default) · checkbox · link (chevron, no control) · icon (icon box + trailing radio)

props.name: aria-describedby
props.description: Extra description, for example the id of a hint. The error message is added to it.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Names the radiogroup. Give this or `aria-labelledby`, or wrap the group in a fieldset with a legend.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Names the radiogroup by another element, for example a heading.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables every row in the group. Disabled rows are skipped by the arrow keys.

props.name: error
props.description: Error message under the list; marks the group invalid and is linked with `aria-describedby`. Announced when it appears.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Marks the group invalid (`aria-invalid`) and gives the rows that are not chosen the error tint. Implied by `error`.

props.name: name
props.description: Name of the group in a form: the chosen value is submitted under it (the radios carry hidden inputs).

props.name: required
props.description: A choice is required before the form can be submitted (`aria-required`, and native validation on submit).

props.name: aria-describedby
props.description: Extra description, for example the id of a hint. The error message is added to it.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Names the radiogroup. Give this or `aria-labelledby`, or wrap the group in a fieldset with a legend.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Names the radiogroup by another element, for example a heading.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables every row in the group. Disabled rows are skipped by the arrow keys.

props.name: error
props.description: Error message under the list; marks the group invalid and is linked with `aria-describedby`. Announced when it appears.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Marks the group invalid (`aria-invalid`) and gives the rows that are not chosen the error tint. Implied by `error`.

props.name: name
props.description: Name of the group in a form: the chosen value is submitted under it (the radios carry hidden inputs).

props.name: required
props.description: A choice is required before the form can be submitted (`aria-required`, and native validation on submit).

props.name: value
props.description: Radio mode: the chosen value. Setting any of `value`, `onValueChange`, `name`, `required`, `disabled`, `invalid` or `error` turns the group into a radiogroup.

parts.name: SelectorItem
parts.description: The bordered row with 12 px corners, all of it except the action one label, so a click anywhere toggles the control. The row takes the indigo tint and a 1.5 px rim when chosen.

parts.name: SelectorItemGroup
parts.description: A vertical stack of rows with an 8 px gap, so several options read as one list.

parts.name: Leading
parts.description: An optional icon, avatar or logo before the text. The slot is at least 32 px wide and centres its content, so text starts at the same x in every row.

parts.name: Icon tile
parts.description: The `icon` prop: a 40 px tile with a tint-indigo fill and the icon in tint-text, with no rim. It sits in the leading slot.

parts.name: Title
parts.description: One line of 14 px medium text. It names the control for assistive technology and is cut with an ellipsis when too long.

parts.name: Description
parts.description: One line of secondary text, 4 px below the title. It describes the control for assistive technology.

parts.name: Badge
parts.description: The `badge` prop: a light pill next to the title, such as Recommended.

parts.name: Metadata
parts.description: Short secondary text before the control, such as a price or a count. It sits inside the label and is plain text, not interactive.

parts.name: Control
parts.description: The radio, checkbox or switch you pass as the control. It is the one tab stop of the row and keeps its own focus ring.

parts.name: Action
parts.description: A secondary button such as Edit. It sits outside the label, so clicking it never toggles the control, and it has its own tab stop.

parts.name: Group error
parts.description: The `error` of a radio group: a 14 px red line under the list with `role="alert"`, linked to the group.

items.text: Use it for choices needing a title and an explanation: delivery methods, plans, a switch setting. For a short label by a box use Checkbox with Label, for button-sized options Radio Button Group.
Pass the matching control: a radio inside a RadioGroup, or a Checkbox or Switch alone. The border follows the control's checked state, so the row needs no props for it.
Keep the title to one line and put the detail in the description. Both are truncated, so long text is cut with an ellipsis.
Put a secondary button in the action slot, not in the title or description. It stays outside the label and has its own tab stop.
Use the error prop for a row that cannot be chosen or must be ticked. It turns the row red, marks the control invalid and links the message to it.
Don't put a link or button in the title or description. The row is one label, and a click on it toggles the control.
Don't mix controls in one list, such as a switch row between radio rows. People read one control as one kind of choice.
Don't use card rows for a long list. Switch to the inline layout, or to a Select, once there are more than about six options.

themingVariables.name: --tint-text-indigo
themingVariables.usedFor: background, border, text · dark, hover, invalid, pressed, selected

components.title: Label
components.description: An accessible label for a form control.

parts.name: Label
parts.description: A native label in a row, 8 px between children, in 14 px medium text. Join it to a control by id, by wrapping the control, or with FieldLabel inside a Field; clicking it focuses the control.

parts.name: Requirement note
parts.description: A short word after the name, Required or Optional, in 12 px tertiary text. It sits inside the label, so it is part of the accessible name and a screen reader reads it too.

parts.name: Control
parts.description: The field the label names: an Input, a Textarea, a Checkbox. A label without a control is just text, and in a Field the label dims when the control is disabled.

items.text: Use a Label for every control with a visible name: above a field, to the left in a settings row, or to the right of a checkbox. Name a group of controls with a Fieldset legend, not a Label.
Join every label to its control: FieldLabel inside a Field, otherwise a matching id and htmlFor. The words then become a click target as large as the row.
Write the label as a short noun (Work email) and put a rule or an example in the helper line below the field. A label is a name, not a sentence.
Mark what is unusual: the optional fields in a mostly required form, the required ones in a mostly optional form. Put the note inside the label so it is read with the name.
Keep a label for a compact control and hide it visually. A search field without a visible label still has a name and a click target for assistive technology.
Keep buttons out of the label. An info tip next to a label is a sibling in the row, so clicking it doesn't focus the field.
Don't use a placeholder as the label. It is gone with the first keystroke and is not announced as a name on every screen reader.
Don't mark required with a colour or an asterisk alone. The word Required is readable by everyone; an asterisk needs an explanation on the page.
Don't leave a label unjoined. Text that looks like a label but has no link to the control gives it no name and no click target.

components.title: Field
components.description: Labelling and validation for a single form control — label, description, and error message.

props.name: actionsRef
props.description: A ref to imperative actions. - `validate`: Validates the field when called.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class applied to the element, or a function that returns a class based on the component's state.

props.name: dirty
props.description: Whether the field's value has been changed from its initial value. Useful when the field state is controlled by an external library.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether the component should ignore user interaction. Takes precedence over the `disabled` prop on the `<Field.Control>` component.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Whether the field is invalid. Useful when the field state is controlled by an external library.

props.name: name
props.description: Identifies the field when a form is submitted. Takes precedence over the `name` prop on the `<Field.Control>` component.

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

props.name: style
props.description: Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state.

props.name: touched
props.description: Whether the field has been touched. Useful when the field state is controlled by an external library.

props.name: validate

parts.name: Field
parts.description: The wrapper of one control: a column with 4 px between its parts. It owns the name, invalid, disabled and validation state, and every part inside reads them.

parts.name: FieldLabel
parts.description: The visible name of the control, in 14 px medium text with 4 px below it. It is linked to the control, so a click on it focuses the control, and it dims with a disabled field.

parts.name: Control
parts.description: The control itself. An Input joins the Field by itself, any other control such as a Textarea joins through FieldControl, and the Field passes it the invalid and described-by attributes.

parts.name: FieldDescription
parts.description: The hint under the control in 12 px tertiary text. It is linked to the control, so a screen reader reads it after the label, and it dims with a disabled field.

parts.name: FieldError
parts.description: The error message in 12 px error text. It shows only while the field is invalid, is linked to the control and is left out while the field is disabled, so hide the hint while it shows.

items.text: Use Field around every control with a label, hint or error. It draws no box; put Fields in a Fieldset for a group, and use Form to send data and take server errors.
Put the label first, then the control, then the hint or the error. A label is a noun (Work email) and a hint is a full sentence.
Give each Field a name when it sits in a Form. The name is how an error you pass to the Form finds its field.
Write the error as an instruction: Enter an email address like name@company.com, not Invalid. Show it after the person leaves the field or sends the form, and keep what they typed.
Render the hint only while there is no error, so the error takes its place. Keep a line of room for the message so the controls below do not jump.
Mark an exception on the label row (Optional), not in the placeholder. A placeholder is gone once the person starts to type.
Don't build the label, hint and error by hand with label, p and ids. You lose the links that Field sets and the state that reaches every part.
Don't put two controls in one Field. The label names one control; two controls need a Fieldset with a legend.
Don't disable only the control and leave the Field enabled. The label and hint then stay at full strength next to a dimmed control.
